input.quote: This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein or unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year.
input.rationale: Section 13 (p0078) provides automatic renewal for successive one-year (not multi-year) terms, with either party — including us as Client — able to prevent renewal on written notice given only 30 days before the end of the then-current year. That meets the preferred position on the material terms: 12-month renewal length and a 30-day customer opt-out, well inside the fallback's 60-day ceiling and far from the 90-day/multi-year walk-away. Two minor sub-elements fall short of the ideal drafting and are noted rather than flagged: there is no Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal, and there is no CPI/3% cap on renewal pricing (Section 6 (p0047) only freezes Hosting Services costs for the first year and adds a most-favoured-rate commitment, so post-year-one uplifts are uncapped). Per the playbook's classification semantics these are not independent deviations; we can raise the reminder and uplift cap as goodwill asks if the renewal economics are negotiated.
